answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost. A wharf stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a saffron...
